feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: The other side of 9/11: Afghans reckon with America's long shadow
entry.summary: It's been nearly 25 years since the start of the U.S- led invasion of Afghanistan. NPR returns to Kabul to see how Afghans, now back under Taliban rule, are coping with the legacy of that 20 year war.

entry.title: Amid war and sanctions, many Iranians are losing their jobs and struggling to get by
entry.summary: Many Iranians lost their jobs because of the war and the U.S. blockade. Now some are even losing their backup jobs as sanctions tighten.

entry.title: The U.S.-Canada trade war is creating a headache for auto-parts makers
entry.summary: For decades, the U.S. and Canadian auto supply chains have been tightly woven together. The trade war is threatening to unravel a complex system.

entry.title: Why gains by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen could push gas prices even higher
entry.summary: A Houthi advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast could help push gas prices up even more as the Iran-backed group also launches attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil facilities.

entry.title: Hong Kong court sentences 3 Tiananmen vigil organizers to prison
entry.summary: The activists were sentenced to about 5 to 7 years in prison in a case widely seen as a barometer of the city's eroding freedoms as Beijing clamps down on dissent.

entry.title: Iran-backed Houthi rebels seize a strategic port and island, opening a new battlefront
entry.summary: The rebel group took over Yemen's port of Mokha, an area vital to controlling shipping through the Red Sea, Houthi and Yemeni officials said. Mokha is about 50 miles from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

entry.title: Amid war and sanctions, unemployment worsens in Iran
entry.summary: As the U.S. war with Iran drags on, Iranians face increasing layoffs and a rising unemployment rate.

entry.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
entry.summary: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.

entry.title: UN peacekeepers give NPR a rare look behind Israeli lines
entry.summary: NPR accompanies UN peacekeepers behind Israeli lines as Israel expands its occupation of South Lebanon following a U.S.-brokered ceasefire.

entry.title: 'I'll never trust them again': Some Afghans who helped the U.S. post-9/11 regret it
entry.summary: Soon after the Sept. 11 attacks, the U.S. launched what would become a 20-year war in Afghanistan. Some Afghans who helped the U.S. prosecute that war regret it.
